COURSE HANDOUT: CS301 - AUTOMATA THEORY AND FORMAL LANGUAGES

Instructor: Dr. Sarah Mitchell
Office: CS Building, Room 304
Email: smitchell@university.edu
Office Hours: Tue/Thu 2:00-4:00 PM

Teaching Assistant: Alex Chen
Email: achen@university.edu

COURSE DESCRIPTION
This course covers the theoretical foundations of computer science, focusing on formal languages, automata theory, and computability. Students will learn to classify languages, design automata, and understand the limits of computation.

TEXTBOOK
- "Introduction to the Theory of Computation" by Michael Sipser, 3rd Edition
- "Automata Theory, Languages, and Computation" by Hopcroft, Motwani, Ullman

GRADING
- Midterm Exam: 30%
- Final Exam: 40%
- Assignments: 20%
- Quizzes: 10%

SCHEDULE
Week 1-2: Introduction, Mathematical Preliminaries, Alphabets, Strings, Languages
Week 3-4: Deterministic Finite Automata (DFA) - Definition, Examples, Design
Week 5-6: Non-deterministic Finite Automata (NFA) - Definition, ε-NFA, Subset Construction
Week 7-8: Regular Expressions - Syntax, Semantics, Conversion to/from FA
Week 9-10: Properties of Regular Languages - Pumping Lemma, Closure Properties, Decision Properties
Week 11-12: DFA Minimization - Table-filling Algorithm, Myhill-Nerode Theorem
Week 13-14: Context-Free Grammars - Definition, Parse Trees, Ambiguity, Normal Forms
Week 15-16: Pushdown Automata - Definition, Equivalence with CFG, Deterministic PDA

MIDSEM SYLLABUS (Weeks 1-12)
- Regular Languages through DFA Minimization
- All of Unit 1

IMPORTANT DATES
- Midterm Exam: October 15, 2024 (90 minutes, 60 marks)
- Assignment 1 Due: September 20
- Assignment 2 Due: October 5
- Assignment 3 Due: November 2

ACADEMIC INTEGRITY
All work must be your own. Collaboration on assignments is limited to discussion of concepts only.
